bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Pay: From Hourly Rate to Annual Salary

If you’re paid by the hour or have a salary offer, converting your rate to an annual figure helps you compare jobs and plan your budget. The standard formula is:

**Annual gross pay ≈ hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

This article assumes a 38-hour week, which is the full-time benchmark used by the Fair Work Ombudsman. If you work different hours, simply adjust the calculation. For example, a 20-hour week would use 20 instead of 38.

We also explain how the National Minimum Wage compares with award rates, how casual loading and superannuation work, and how to estimate your take-home pay using the [take home pay calculator australia gov](/topics/take-home) tool.

### The National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage, set by the Fair Work Commission, is the minimum pay for employees not covered by an award or agreement. From 1 July 2026, it is **$26.44 per hour**, or **$1,004.90 per week** for 38 hours. This applies to most adult employees.

However, many workers are covered by an industry or occupation award, which often sets higher minimum rates. For example, the General Retail Industry Award may have different rates for different classifications. To find your correct minimum, check the [pay guides](/blog) or the Fair Work Ombudsman website.

The Australian Bureau of Statistics publishes **Average Weekly Earnings**, which for May 2026 was **$2,083.70 per week** for full-time adult ordinary time. This is an average across all industries and states, not the median for your specific job. Your actual pay may be higher or lower depending on your role, experience, and location.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of their base hourly rate to compensate for unpaid leave entitlements. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is **$33.05 per hour** ($26.44 × 1.25). If you are casual, always use the base rate (without loading) in the calculator, then tick the “casual loading” checkbox. Never type a rate that already includes loading.

Superannuation is paid on top of your gross earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is **12% of ordinary earnings**, up to a maximum contribution base of **$270,830 per year**. For example, if your annual gross is $60,000, your employer must pay an extra $7,200 into your super fund. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional cost for the employer.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your take-home pay is what you receive after tax and the Medicare levy are deducted. The 2026-27 resident tax rates are:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

The Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. Note that the 2026-27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed at the time of this guide, so the calculator uses the 2025-26 single reduction thresholds. HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not included in this estimate.

To see how much you’ll actually keep, use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool. It applies the tax brackets and Medicare levy to your annual gross income.

### Using the Timesheet Tool

The [timesheet](/) on this site lets you enter your base hourly rate. A checkbox adds 25% casual loading automatically. The tool then calculates:

- Weekly pay (hourly rate × hours per week)
- Fortnightly pay (weekly × 2)
- Annual gross (weekly × 52)
- Estimated tax and Medicare levy
- Superannuation (12% on top, up to the maximum contribution base)

Remember, the annual figure assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026-27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold.

This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax. For personalised advice, consult a qualified professional or the Australian Taxation Office.

### Why Compare the National Minimum Wage and an Award?

If you are not covered by an award, the National Minimum Wage is your legal minimum. But if your job falls under an award, your minimum rate may be higher. For example, a hospitality award might set a higher rate for evening work. Always check your award classification.

The [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page has more details on the National Minimum Wage and how it applies. For award-specific rates, refer to the Fair Work Ombudsman’s pay guides.

By understanding the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates, you can ensure you are paid correctly. Use the take home pay calculator australia gov to compare your current or offered rate with the relevant minimums.

### Final Tips

- Always use your base hourly rate (before casual loading) in the calculator.
- If you work more than 38 hours, your award may require overtime or penalty rates. This calculator does not include those.
- Super is paid on top of your gross earnings, not deducted from your pay.
- The take home pay calculator australia gov is a useful starting point, but always verify with official sources for your specific situation.
